text: The 2022 loss in native forest (0.5 ha) was caused by deforestation, as confirmed by three independent datasets. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset detected the loss in 2022, while the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 reference confirmed that the area was fully forested in 2020. The Uruguayan national forest map (MGAP 2021) classified the lost area as native forest, with no planted species present. The loss was concentrated in a single event (0.6 ha total), with 0.2 ha occurring in small patches (<0.5 ha) that were excluded from the final count. No further deforestation was observed after 2022. The cause appears to be anthropogenic, though the exact activity (e.g., agriculture, logging) is not specified in the data.
